title: Burns & Scalds
summary: Cool the burn with cool running water as soon as possible, remove jewellery, then cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for serious burns
when: Large burns, or burns to the face, hands, feet, genitals or across joints
Deep burns (white, leathery or charred) or burns that go all the way round a limb
Breathing difficulty, or burns from smoke/fire in an enclosed space (airway burns)
Burns in babies, young children, older adults or anyone who seems unwell

steps.title: Stop the burning
steps.text: Get them away from the heat source. Stop, drop and roll if clothing is on fire. Make sure you are safe.

steps.title: Cool the burn
steps.text: Cool with cool or lukewarm running water as soon as possible.
points: European Resuscitation Council: cool for at least 20 minutes
AHA / Red Cross: cool for at least 10 minutes
Keep the rest of the person warm to avoid hypothermia, especially children

steps.title: Remove jewellery and clothing near the burn
steps.text: Gently remove rings, watches and clothing near the burn before swelling starts, unless they are stuck to the skin.

steps.title: Chemical burns
steps.text: Brush off dry chemicals (wearing gloves), then flush with large amounts of running water. Remove contaminated clothing. Note the chemical name for responders.

steps.title: Cover the burn
steps.text: After cooling, cover loosely with cling film (laid on, not wrapped tightly) or a clean, non-fluffy dressing.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Watch for signs of shock and breathing problems. Seek medical advice for anything other than a small, superficial burn.

warningSigns: Hoarse voice, soot around the mouth or nose, singed nasal hair, coughing – possible airway burn
Burn larger than the casualty's palm (in a child, any blistering burn)
doNot: Do not use ice, iced water, butter, creams, ointments or toothpaste
Do not remove anything stuck to the burn
Do not use fluffy dressings or adhesive plasters on the burn
Do not wrap cling film tightly around a limb

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
